newsitem.title: THAILAND: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - Oct 17.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - Oct 17.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Thai press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Newin Chidchob, former member of parliament, and his associates are still struggling to find a party that will accept them, and they may lose the chance to seek re-election. Newin, according to a source, was planning to buy a registered political party that has been inactive for five million baht in order to remain politically alive. (THE NATION) (BANGKOK POST)

- Floodwaters from the swollen Chao Phya River have inundated areas of inner Bangkok, after frustrated residents tore down embankments in the first case of disorder sparked by flood-induced tension this year. Bangkok governor Bhichit Rattakul has warned Bangkok residents to be prepared for the severest flooding of the year from October 24-27. (THE NATION) (BANGKOK POST)

- Commercial banks are trying to increase the amount of deposits during the last quarter of this year through raising interest rates. Foreign banks have forecast that rates will rise by another 0.5 basis points. The trend is against the central bank's policy which wants to see the rates to be cut. (MANAGER)

- Tenants have filed charges with the civil court against SCB Park Plaza's developer, Mahisorn Co Ltd, demanding six million baht in compensation. They charged the developer with cheating and breaching rental contract. (BANGKOK POST)

- Bank of Thailand governor Rerngchai Marakanond has said up to seven foreign-bank representative offices operating under the Bangkok International Banking Facility scheme will be allowed to upgrade to full branches before the election. He says approval can be extended before the formation of the new administration, while the issuing of three banking licences to local operators will be suspended due to bribery allegations. (THE NATION)
